column2: Can Frank steal a parked Cortina from outside the chip shop with the owner watching from the window, and will the owner describe both Frank and the car to the police?
Can Frank drag a driver out of his car at a red light, and do other drivers and pedestrians react, run, or call it in?
What happens if Frank steals a car and the owner's wife reports it, so a patrol car later spots the number plate on the docks road?
Can Frank swap number plates between two cars in a lock-up and then drive past a constable who is looking for the first plate?
Can Frank outrun a panda car through the Hook's back streets, park in a yard, and have the police lose him but still search the area?
What happens if Frank drives a minicab with a bleeding passenger in the back and a patrol car pulls alongside?
Can Frank mount the pavement to escape a chase, and will pedestrians he scatters remember his face and the cab's livery?
Can Frank hit a lamp post hard enough to cripple the cab, and will his own drivers refuse to take it out until it is fixed?
Can Frank ram a rival gang's van off the dock road and into the water, and what do the dockers on the quay say afterwards?
What happens if Frank runs over a tramp sleeping in a shop doorway by accident, and a witness at the bus stop saw the cab?
Can Frank torch a rival's car in a car park at night, and will the fire brigade's arrival bring the police to question the neighbours?
Can Frank hotwire a van at the docks and drive it into a warehouse yard without the night watchman challenging him?
What happens if Frank starts a fistfight in the cafe, and the cook, two customers and the waitress all take different sides?
Can Frank snatch a handbag from a woman at the bus shelter, run, and be chased by a passing man who decides to be a hero?
Can Frank rob the newsagent's till at closing time, and does the owner give a different description to the police than the cleaner does?
What happens if Frank robs a corner shop while the shopkeeper's brother, who is a docker, is sitting in the back room?
Can Frank walk into the post office wearing a mask and be recognised anyway by his voice or his gait?
Can Frank go on a rampage with a cosh through a street market, and does the town shut its shutters and stay indoors for days?
What happens if Frank beats up a man on the high street in front of forty people, and none of them calls the police but all of them gossip?
Can Frank kick a man who is already on the ground, and will the town talk about it differently than a fair fight?
Can Frank pick a pocket on a crowded bus and have the victim feel it a stop later and accuse the wrong passenger?
Can Frank knock a man out, drag him into the cab's boot, and drive him to the canal without anyone on the street noticing?
What happens if Frank leaves a body in the boot of a minicab and a mechanic is asked to look at the car the next day?
Can Frank steal a police panda car while the constables are inside a house, and what happens when he drives it into the Hook?
Can Frank wear a stolen police helmet and tunic to walk through a cordon at the docks?
Can Frank cause a diversion, like a false alarm at a warehouse, to pull the patrols away before a break-in elsewhere?
What happens if Frank phones in a tip from a phone box about a rival, and the call is traced to that box with a witness nearby?
Can Frank break a rival's shop window at three in the morning and be seen by a milkman on his round?
Can Frank sell a fence in a back room a stolen car stereo, and will the price drop if the fence has too many already?
Can Frank break into a tobacconist's through the roof, and does the alarm bell bring neighbours to their windows?
What happens if Frank escapes a police chase on foot over a canal bridge, but loses his cap and a witness picks it up?
Can Frank hide in the cab office with the lights off while two constables knock on the door, and will his dispatcher cover for him?
Can Frank bribe a constable on the beat to look the other way during a break-in, and does that constable then ask for more next week?
What happens if Frank is arrested after a chase, spends a night in the cells, and his crew has to decide whether to bail him or let him sweat?
Can Frank get a wanted description changed by repainting the cab, changing his coat and cutting his hair, and when does the town stop looking for him?
Can Frank hold up a security van on the dock road with a crew of three, and will each crew member behave differently under pressure?
Can Frank use a stolen lorry to block the dock road and stop a rival's delivery from reaching the warehouse?
What happens if Frank drives a getaway car and one of his crew sits in the back wounded and panicking, and the wounded man begs him to stop at a doctor's?
Can Frank climb onto the roof of a terrace and jump between houses to escape police, and will the residents complain about the noise?
Can Frank shove a pursuing constable into a skip or a hedge to slow him, and does the constable remember it as an assault?
Can Frank hijack a delivery lorry on the road to the docks, take the load to the lock-up, and sell it on over several days without being traced?
What happens if Frank speeds through the market in the cab on a Saturday and the traders hurl things at him afterwards whenever he passes?
Can Frank take a hostage at the docks, such as a ship's clerk, to get past the gate guards, and what does the clerk say afterwards?
Can Frank set fire to the cab office's own back room for a fake insurance claim, and will the loss adjuster ask the neighbours questions?
Can Frank scare a witness into silence by turning up at her front door and standing outside for an evening, and will her neighbours notice and talk?
What happens if Frank steals the car of a local councillor and finds papers in the glove box that he can later use as leverage?
Can Frank tail a rival's car at night with the headlights off through the Hook, and will the rival's driver notice and take a different route?
Can Frank park the cab across a side street to trap a patrol car in the alley behind the cafe, and what do the constables do?
What happens if Frank smashes through a level crossing barrier ahead of a goods train to lose a chase, and the signalman reports the cab?
Can Frank escape by hiding the car in a lock-up that belongs to someone he has bribed, and does the lock-up owner keep quiet when the police ask?
Can Frank take a cab full of paying passengers on a wild chase by accident, and will they complain, panic, or demand to be let out?
Can Frank wear the same suit for a fortnight and have the barber, the cafe owner and his crew comment on the smell and the stains?
What happens if Frank gets soaked in a November downpour on the docks and then sits in the cab for hours without changing, does he catch a cold and cough through conversations?
Can Frank buy a second-hand overcoat from a market stall and have people recognise it as a dead man's coat?
Can Frank wear a donkey jacket and hard hat to walk onto the docks and be taken for a stevedore by the gatekeeper?
Can Frank get a haircut and a wet shave at the barber on a Saturday morning and have regulars notice the difference at Mickey's that afternoon?
What happens if Frank turns up to a funeral for a local docker in a bright shirt, and do the mourners remember it?
Can Frank stand in the queue at the chip shop at lunchtime and be served in turn, or does the owner wave him ahead because of his reputation?
Can Frank sleep through the afternoon in the flat above the office and be woken by the landlady knocking about the rent?
What happens if Frank skips meals for two days while working double shifts, does he get shaky and mutter in conversation?
Can Frank wash his own shirts in the bath and hang them on a line across the back yard to dry, and what happens if it rains?
Can Frank bring a fresh pot of tea and a plate of toast to the night radio girl at the cab office and have her remember it at the end of the week?
Can Frank go to the Sunday service at the local church and sit at the back, and does the vicar greet him by name the next time he passes?
What happens if Frank always pays his tab at the newsagent on Friday, and does the owner start keeping his paper aside and mention him kindly to others?
Can Frank give a pensioner a free lift home from the post office on pension day, and will she tell her friends at the tea room by the market?
Can Frank stand on the sea wall at dawn and smoke a cigarette while a docker tells him about the old days before the cranes?
What happens if Frank is seen leaving the flat of a married woman at six in the morning, and does her husband hear of it by dinner time?
Can Frank return a lost wallet to a stranger at the bus station without taking the cash, and does that stranger spread the word?
Can Frank refuse a bribe from a rival and have the whole street know he is a man who cannot be bought?
Can Frank apologise in person to a shopkeeper he threatened last week and have her take back what she told her neighbours?
What happens if Frank breaks a promise to a driver to cover his Christmas shift, does the driver tell the other drivers and does loyalty drop across the office?
Can Frank keep a handwritten notebook of favours owed and favours due that the player reads and the townspeople also seem to track?
Can Frank tell a rival gang man to his face in the street that he will meet him at the cranes at midnight, and does the man turn up with others?
What happens if Frank hits a man who is already on the ground, do onlookers lose respect even if the man had it coming?
Can Frank walk away from an insult in the cafe in front of his crew, and do they read it as wisdom or as weakness?
Can Frank spare a beaten rival's life on the quayside and have the rival's men later come to him because of it?
Can Frank take the blame in front of the police for something a young driver did, and does that driver's loyalty turn to devotion?
Can Frank cross the road to avoid an old enemy in the market and have bystanders notice the avoidance?
Can Frank stand at his late uncle's grave with a bunch of flowers on the anniversary and have an old friend of Mickey's join him and talk?
Can Frank find his uncle's old diaries in a drawer and read them across several evenings, learning names and debts as a slow reveal?
Can Frank sit in the corner of the cafe for a whole morning doing nothing but drinking tea and watching the street, and learn who comes and goes?
Can Frank wait at the bus shelter in the drizzle with a newspaper and eavesdrop on a woman telling a friend about the landlord's visitors?
Can Frank carry a stranger's heavy suitcase up the station steps and be told a piece of local rumour in thanks?
What happens if Frank dresses as a rent collector and knocks on doors in a block of flats, do people answer and can he learn who is behind on their payments?
Can Frank grow a moustache over a few weeks and have the town react to the change in his face, including the police who have his description?
Can Frank take his cab to the car wash on a Sunday and have the lad there remember to keep the back seat clean for fares who complain?
What happens if Frank leaves a cigarette burning in the cab ashtray overnight and a smell of smoke puts off a fussy regular in the morning?
Can Frank ask a pensioner on the pier for a light and strike up a half-hour talk about the war, and does he see the old man again next week at the same bench?
Can Frank join the dockers queuing for the early shift at the gate and work an honest day to earn local respect, then return to the office tired and filthy?
What happens if Frank offers a cigarette to a nervous witness before asking a question and does she open up more than if he had just demanded?
Can Frank leave the flat unlocked while he works and come back to find his landlady has tidied up and read his letters?
Can Frank repair a broken window at the cafe himself on a Sunday morning because he knocked it out in a scuffle, and have the owner forgive him?
What happens if Frank is late three times in a row for a standing Thursday supper at his aunt's, and does she stop setting his place?
Can Frank get a hot-water bottle, a kettle and a bag of coal into the office on the first freezing night of December and have the drivers thank him for it?
Can Frank take a night driver aside after a cruel remark and put right a grudge between two crew members, and do the others see how he handles it?
Can Frank wear a black armband for a week after a crewman dies and be treated differently on the street?
Can Frank tell an elderly woman he is Mickey's nephew and hear a different story of Mickey than the one his crew tells?
What happens if Frank is always seen at the same corner table in the cafe at ten each morning, do people start to turn up there to ask him for favours?
Can Frank buy a bunch of flowers from the stall by the bus station and give them to a widow whose husband died owing money to him, and does she cancel her fear of him?
Can Frank walk the length of the Hook at closing time on a Saturday night and see each shopkeeper pull down their shutters in a routine he can learn?
Can Frank have a quiet wake for a dead driver in the back room of the office with tea, sandwiches and the man's family, and have the district talk about it for weeks?
What happens if Frank lets the office go to seed for a month, with unwashed mugs and bills pinned on the wall, do customers start taking their trade to the rival firm?
Can Frank ring a customer back from the phone box on the corner after the cab office line goes dead, and does the coin box swallow his ten pence if he talks too long?
What happens if Frank is ten pence short at the phone box and asks a passing woman for change, and she later mentions him to her neighbour?
Can Frank queue at the dole office on a Tuesday morning and overhear the clerk and the claimants talking about who has been caught working on the side?
Can Frank sign on at the dole office while running the cab office, and what happens if a neighbour tells the clerk he has been seen driving?
What happens if Frank is seen by someone from the office buying a poll tax summons envelope's worth of stamps at the post office, and does the town read anything into his debts?
Can Frank pay a neighbour's poll tax bill in cash, and does the street remember him as the man who sorted it?
Can Frank refuse to pay his own poll tax and receive a court summons through the door at Mickey's, with a bailiff turning up weeks later?
Can Frank hide a van full of takings behind the cab office when a bailiff comes to the door about the unpaid poll tax, and does the bailiff come back with a policeman?
Can Frank take a minicab fare to the ferry terminal at dawn and pick up a returning crew member whose name he has to find out from the foreman?
What happens if Frank drives a passenger to the ferry terminal and the last sailing has just gone, leaving the man shouting on the quayside?
Can Frank wait on the quay in thick sea fog for a delivery, and does the fog stop the police lamp from seeing him from the far wall?
Can Frank sit out a gale in the cab office while the docks shut down, and do the dockers drift in to Mickey's to get out of the rain and talk?
What happens if Frank drives the cab over the wet cobbles by the fish quay in November and skids into a stack of crates?
Can Frank walk down a terraced street at six in the morning and hear the knocker-up or the milk float, and does the milkman remember who he saw on the corner?
Can Frank leave a bag with the woman in the corner shop to collect later, and will she look inside?
Can Frank buy a packet of cigarettes on tick at the corner shop, and does the shopkeeper start chalking up what he owes in the back book?
What happens if Frank asks the corner shop owner to stop selling a rival's papers, or to put a card in the window for Mickey's cabs?
Can Frank put a postcard advertising the cab office in the newsagent's window, and does a rival firm take it down overnight?
Can Frank get a slow cold meal from the chip shop on a Friday night and find it queued out the door, with people talking about the news from the docks?
Can Frank stand in the chip shop queue and hear two women talk about the man who got his face cut near the lock gates last week?
Can Frank go to the launderette on a rainy Sunday and pass information through a woman folding sheets who only talks when the machines are loud?
What happens if Frank leaves his bloodied shirt in a launderette dryer and a woman there notices the stain?
Can Frank hang his washing out on the line behind the cab office and have a neighbour comment on a missing sheet?
Can Frank borrow a cup of sugar from the next terrace door and get invited in for a cup of tea he could use to learn the street's secrets?
Can Frank sit in a front room with a gas fire on the meter and talk to an old woman who lets him charge her meter with his own coins?
What happens if Frank puts fifty pence into a neighbour's gas meter and she tells the rest of the street how kind he is?
Can Frank take a night shift in the cab office and handle a stream of tired, rowdy late fares after the cinema lets out, and does a rude passenger get a clip round the ear from the radio operator?
Can Frank refuse to pick up a fare because the street is known for trouble, and does the caller go to a rival firm and tell people Mickey's is unreliable?
Can Frank give a stranger in the rain a lift to the bus station for nothing and have that stranger turn up later at a worse moment?
Can Frank take a cab fare to the hospital in the middle of the night and be asked by the nurse to wait outside for a man who may not come out?
Can Frank wait in a night bus shelter on a freezing morning and chat to a night shift cleaner on her way home who sees everything on her route?
What happens if Frank gets onto the last bus home with no change and the conductor lets him on or throws him off?
Can Frank ride the early workers' bus and learn from the dockers on board when the next shipment is due?
Can Frank use the town library on a Saturday to look up old newspapers about his uncle's death, and does the librarian remember what he asked for?
Can Frank read the local evening paper in the cab office and find a story about a fight he was part of, written with the wrong details?
Can Frank ring the evening paper from a phone box and give a false tip about a crime, and does a reporter turn up at the address?
Can Frank buy a second-hand television from a market stall and have the stallholder ask no questions about where the aerial goes?
Can Frank sell a stolen video recorder on the market on a Saturday morning, and does a trader on the next stall mark him as a fence?
What happens if Frank is seen in the covered market handing a brown envelope to the butcher, and the next shopper repeats it in the queue?
Can Frank get his hair cut at the barber's on the high street and hear which men have been in lately with injuries?
Can Frank wear a donkey jacket and a flat cap to blend in with the dockers, and do they notice he has never worked a shift?
Can Frank walk onto the docks at the shift change in the morning and be mistaken for a casual labourer asking for a day's work?
Can Frank bribe a gatekeeper at the dock gate with a carton of cigarettes to be let in after hours, and does the next shift's gateman ask about it?
Can Frank sit in the transport cafe by the docks with a mug of strong tea and a bacon roll and get the lorry drivers to talk about a cargo gone astray?
What happens if Frank is seen parked for an hour outside the closed bingo-free social hall on the estate, and rumours start about what he was waiting for?
Can Frank attend a funeral for a docker and stand with the family at the back, and does the town read anything into who comes to pay respects?
Can Frank go to the wedding reception in the church hall of a local family and be refused entry because he is the wrong sort, or let in because of a favour he did?
Can Frank join a street collection for a dead man's widow by knocking on doors, and does the street think better of him if he gives a big sum?
Can Frank watch the bonfire night fire on the waste ground on the fifth of November, and have someone use the noise and the crowd to cover a deal?
Can Frank take a fare to the Christmas lights switch-on on the high street and be stuck there in a crowd, with people recognising the cab and tapping the window?
Can Frank get a seasonal job for a cousin at the sorting office in December, and does the cousin start passing information about parcels?
Can Frank walk past a queue of people outside the electricity board showroom on the day the bills arrive and hear what they are saying about money?
Can Frank watch a power cut take out the whole terrace one winter evening and use the dark to slip into a house without being seen by the street?
Can Frank ask one of his drivers to say Frank was in the cab office all Tuesday night, and will that driver hold to it when a detective leans on him alone in an interview room?
What happens if two of Frank's alibi witnesses tell the police different times, say one says he left at nine and the other says half ten?
Can Frank plant a stolen wallet in a rival's coat pocket at the cafe and then tip off a constable to search him?
Can Frank photograph the bent detective taking an envelope in the multi-storey car park and later use the prints to make him drop a case?
What happens if the bent detective learns Frank has those photographs and decides it is safer to have Frank put away?
Can Frank feed a piece of false information to only one member of his crew, and work out who the informer is by seeing whether the police act on it?
If Frank finds out which driver is informing, can he keep him on and feed the police lies through him instead of getting rid of him?
Can Frank lend money to a struggling corner shop owner, and then call the debt in by asking him to look the other way when a van is unloaded behind his shop at night?
What happens if a man who owes Frank money skips town, and can Frank find out from his landlady or his ex-wife where he went?
Can Frank buy up another man's debts from a rival loan shark and become the one he owes?
Can Frank learn from his uncle Mickey's old ledger who owed Mickey favours, and go round collecting on them?
What happens if someone from Mickey's past turns up at the cab office claiming Mickey owed him, and is he telling the truth?
Can Frank find out how his uncle actually died by asking the right people in the right order, and does anyone lie to protect themselves?
Can Frank tell a rival gang leader that the other gang grassed him up, and will the two gangs turn on each other if he is believed?
What happens if Frank's lie about the rival gang is later contradicted by someone who was actually there?
Can Frank catch a dock foreman having an affair and threaten to tell his wife unless he lets Frank's lads onto the quay after dark?
What happens if Frank's blackmail victim decides he would rather confess to his wife than keep paying, and then goes to the police?
Can Frank burn a rival's minicab office at night and make it look like the rival did it himself for the insurance?
Can Frank wear a rival crew member's distinctive jacket while doing a job so that witnesses describe the wrong man to the police?
If witnesses wrongly name an innocent neighbour for something Frank did, can Frank let him take the fall, and does the town ever learn the truth?
Can Frank go to the police himself as a witness and give a false description that sends them after one of his enemies?
What happens if a loyal crew member is arrested and offered a lighter sentence to give evidence against Frank?
Can Frank pay a solicitor to visit his arrested man in the cells and quietly remind him what happens to people who talk?
Can Frank look after the wife of a crew member who is on remand, paying her rent, so that the man stays loyal inside?
What happens if Frank stops paying that wife's rent, and does the man in prison hear about it from visitors?
Can Frank test a new recruit by leaving cash in the office drawer and watching whether he takes any?
Can Frank order one of his crew to beat up someone the crew member grew up with, and will he refuse, warn the target, or do it and resent Frank?
What happens if Frank's most trusted man is quietly approached by a rival who offers him more money, and can Frank notice the signs?
Can Frank arrange to meet a rival in a quiet lock-up to make peace, and set up an ambush there instead?
If Frank breaks a truce he made in front of witnesses, does the rest of the Hook's underworld stop trusting his word?
Can Frank hide a body's worth of evidence, say a bloodied coat and a cosh, in the harbour, and could a diver or a dredger bring it back up weeks later?
What happens if a witness to an assault Frank committed moves away, and later comes back when the police reopen the case?
Can Frank intimidate a witness into changing her statement, and will the detective notice that her story suddenly changed?
Can Frank keep a ledger of who owes him what, and what happens if a rival or the police get hold of that ledger?
Can Frank arrange for a rival to be seen near a warehouse just before Frank's men rob it, using a fake phone call to lure him there?
Can Frank ring the police from a phone box anonymously, and can they trace that the call came from the box outside his own office?
What happens if Frank's ex-girlfriend, who knows about a crime he did years ago in another town, arrives in Meridian?
Can Frank make someone believe he has evidence against them when he actually has nothing, and does a bluff work better on some people than others?
Can Frank discover that a quiet old man on the estate was once a notorious armed robber, and recruit him for advice on a job?
Can Frank set up a fence in a second-hand shop, and what happens when a customer recognises his own stolen radio in the window?
If Frank does someone a genuine kindness, like getting a thug off the back of a widow, will that widow later refuse to identify him to the police?
Can Frank frame a corrupt councillor's driver for theft so that the councillor has to come to Frank to make it go away?
What happens if two of Frank's crew fall out over a woman and one starts telling outsiders Frank's business out of spite?
Can Frank put a crew member he no longer trusts on a job with a planted weakness, so that he gets caught instead of Frank?
Can Frank play the bent detective and an honest detective off against each other by giving each a different version of the same story?
What happens if the honest detective realises the bent one is on Frank's payroll, and does she go to her superiors or come to Frank?
Can Frank hand a rival over to the police as a grass in exchange for them ignoring his own operation for a month?
If the town learns Frank grassed on a rival, will his own people still trust him or will the word "grass" follow him round the Hook?
Can Frank take the blame for something a loyal crew member did, doing a short stretch on remand, and come out with that man's loyalty for life?
What happens if a driver who saw Frank leave a crime scene in a cab keeps quiet for weeks, then starts asking for money?
Can Frank arrange an alibi by being seen picking up a fare across town at the very time his crew is doing a job at the docks?
Can Frank forge an entry in the cab office's job book to show a fare he never drove, and will a detective think to check it against the passenger?

Can Frank refuse to answer anything in a taped interview at the police station, say "no comment" to every question, and walk out when the custody clock runs out because the CID have nothing but suspicion?
Can Frank ask for the duty solicitor when he is booked in by the custody sergeant, and does the solicitor take him aside and tell him to keep quiet because the witness statement is weak?
What happens if Frank is held for questioning at the station overnight: does the crew carry on running Mickey's without him, or does a rival take the chance to lean on his drivers?
Can Frank stand in an identity parade at the station and hope the shopkeeper who saw him picks out the wrong man from the line of volunteers?

What happens if Frank gets a crew member to warn off the only witness before the identity parade, and the witness then refuses to attend: do the police drop the case or charge Frank with intimidating a witness?
Can Frank turn up at an identity parade with a fresh haircut and his moustache shaved off, and does the witness still pick him out?
Can Frank become a police informant for the bent detective, feeding him tips on a rival gang so the rival gets raided instead of him?
What happens if the town finds out Frank has been passing names to the CID: does word spread that he is a grass, and do people stop talking in front of him?
Can Frank work out which of his own drivers is a police informant by telling each of them a different false story and seeing which one the police act on?
When uniformed officers do house-to-house enquiries along a terrace after a stabbing near the docks, can Frank follow behind and knock on the same doors to find out who told the police what?
Can Frank pay a neighbour to tell the house-to-house officers that she saw a stranger in a donkey jacket running the other way?
Can Frank give a false alibi to the police, saying he was driving a fare all evening, and do they check the cab office booking book and ask the fare?
What happens if Frank's alibi witness gets nervous and changes her story when a detective visits her a second time?
Can Frank burn the jacket he wore during a fight on waste ground behind the warehouses, so the police cannot match the fibres or blood on it?
If Frank leaves fingerprints on a shop counter during a robbery, can the police match them days later, and does it matter whether Frank already has his prints on file from an old arrest?
Can Frank wear gloves to break into a bookkeeper's office, and does the scenes of crime officer then find nothing but glove marks?

What happens if Frank's blood is left at the scene after he cuts his hand smashing a window: can the police use the blood group to narrow it down to him, given it is 1990 and DNA tests are rare and slow?
Can Frank wash his cab out after giving a bleeding man a lift, and will the police still find traces if they impound the car?
Can Frank get a car seized by the police back from the pound by sending someone with forged papers?

What happens if the Crown Prosecution Service decides there is not enough evidence and drops the charge against Frank's crew member: does the arresting detective hold a grudge and come after Frank instead?
Can Frank pay a solicitor to get a remanded crew member out on bail at the magistrates' court, and what happens if the crew member skips bail?
Can Frank visit a crew member held on remand and find out what he told the police, or is the visit watched?
What happens if one of Frank's crew is arrested and the detective offers him a lighter charge to give evidence against Frank: can the crew member turn Queen's evidence?
Can Frank get word to an arrested crew member through his solicitor to keep his mouth shut, and does that put the solicitor at risk?
Can Frank make friends with the local beat bobby, give him free cab rides and tea at the office, so the constable looks the other way on small things?
What happens if the beat constable on foot patrol sees Frank loitering outside a jeweller's three nights running: does he stop Frank and note his name in his pocketbook?
Can the police stop and search Frank in the street on suspicion, and what happens if he is carrying a cosh in his coat at the time?
Can Frank hand his knife to a passer-by just before a constable searches him, and does the passer-by then tell the police?
What happens if Frank runs from a constable who stops him: does the officer radio for help, and do panda cars start cruising the Hook looking for him?
Can Frank hide in a stranger's back yard while police search the streets, and does the householder give him up or keep quiet out of fear?
Can Frank report a crime himself, going into the front counter at the station to tell the desk sergeant about a rival's stolen goods in a lock-up?
Can Frank write an anonymous letter to the police about a rival's hidden stash, and do they act on it without a named witness?
What happens if Frank bribes the bent detective to lose a witness statement: does the case collapse, and does anyone at the station notice the paperwork is missing?
Can Frank get the bent detective to tip him off before a police raid on Mickey's, so he can clear the back room in time?
What happens if the bent detective is himself investigated by an outside force for corruption: does he try to save himself by giving up Frank?
Can Frank secretly record the bent detective taking a bribe and use the tape to control him?
Can Frank frame a rival by planting stolen goods in his car and then tipping off the police with a phone call from a call box?
What happens if Frank uses the same phone box near the cab office for every anonymous tip-off: can the police work out who is calling?
Can Frank buy stolen goods from a thief and then find the police calling at Mickey's because the thief named him when he was nicked?
What happens if a witness picks Frank out from photographs in the mugshot album at the station: is that enough to arrest him, or do the police need more?
Can Frank get a crew member to confess to a crime Frank committed, and do the police believe him if his account does not match the scene?
What happens if Frank is charged and goes to the magistrates' court: does the game play out the hearing, and can witnesses fail to turn up and get the case thrown out?
Can Frank persuade a witness to say in court that she was not wearing her glasses that night, so her identification falls apart?
What happens if the police put an observation post in the flat above the newsagent opposite Mickey's: can Frank notice the curtains twitching and spot the watchers?
Can Frank spot an unmarked police car following his cab and lose it in the back streets of the Hook?
Can Frank find out that his office phone is tapped and use it to feed the police a false meeting time while the real deal goes ahead elsewhere?
What happens if the CID hold a press appeal in the local paper with a photofit that looks a bit like Frank: do townspeople start looking at him differently and phoning the incident room?
Can Frank get a description of himself wrong on purpose by wearing a borrowed coat and a flat cap, so witnesses describe a different man?
What happens if a witness tells the police she saw Frank's minicab, with its office number on the door, parked outside a house that was burgled?
Can Frank swap the number plates on a cab before a job so that a witness who notes the registration sends the police to the wrong car?
What happens if the police arrest the wrong man for something Frank did: does the town gossip about it, and can Frank let him take the blame or quietly get him released?
